dimension_description: This first-pass entropy scale focuses on entropy change, not total entropy and not raw microstate counts. That makes the dimension much more concrete: each item is a process like erasing a bit, melting ice, or vaporizing water. Temperature and process definitions matter a lot here, so qualifiers are especially important.

items.description: A single protein folding event sits at the frontier where chemistry becomes biology. The molecule is small, but its shape matters enough to decide whether it can bind, catalyze, or signal. This is the first place on the scale where one molecule's conformation starts to matter more than a bulk sample.

items.description: RNA does not need to be protein-sized to matter. Even a short hairpin loop can flip between folded and unfolded states, and that switch is one of the cleanest examples of a structure that is small enough to be molecular yet organized enough to carry information.

items.description: A single base pair is too small to look dramatic, but that is exactly why it is useful here. DNA spends part of its life in a breathing, flickering state, and those brief openings are part of how replication and repair reach the sequence underneath.

items.description: Gene regulation often turns on one protein docking event at a specific stretch of DNA. That makes the entropy change tiny in absolute terms, but the biological effect can be outsized because a single binding event can alter which genes are active.

items.name: Transcription factor binding to DNA
items.summary_short: A protein landing on a DNA site is the kind of molecular switch that changes which genes get heard.

items.description: Viruses are good scale anchors because they are built by self-assembly rather than by broad metabolism. A capsid snaps together from many pieces at once, which makes the entropy bookkeeping feel more like organized construction than ordinary chemistry.

items.name: Virus capsid assembly
items.summary_short: A viral shell self-assembling from many proteins is a tiny system with a very large organizational payoff.

items.description: Binary fission is a dramatic biological event even though the entropy change is still microscopic on the everyday scale. The point is not that the number is big, but that a whole cell can reorganize itself and split while staying far below any melting or freezing benchmark.

items.description: This is a good middle ground between pure molecular binding and full cellular behavior. One signal arriving at the right receptor can start a cascade, so a small entropy change can carry a surprisingly large amount of biological consequence.

items.description: Fermentation is one of the rare biological processes that is both chemically precise and immediately familiar. The same pathway that powers yeast also leaves visible bubbles, heat, and flavor, which makes the entropy change feel physical rather than abstract.

items.description: A fruit fly is tiny enough to hold the biological part of this scale together. It is a whole animal, not a molecule or a cell, yet warming it by a degree still sits far below anything kitchen-sized. That makes it a good anchor for the jump from molecular biology to animal bodies.
